narrative: Filed as a leading-indicator finding, not a call to act now: _resolve_horizontal works and is tested (both real Godot suites and the reachability sweep pass), and no refactor happens on the strength of this finding alone. Named as the first refactor candidate for when this function is NEXT touched for any other reason -- at that point, bringing its complexity down from 24 toward the rest of the corpus (median 1, fence 6.0) is an acceptance condition of that change, not a separate project. The director's own initial framing ("the four bugs... lived in the most complex function") was checked against the real source before this event was filed and found to overstate the scope -- only 1 of the 4 lived directly in _resolve_horizontal; this event states the narrower, verified claim rather than the stronger one, consistent with this quality instrument's own reason to exist: reaching a plausible conclusion is not the same as verifying it.
observation: tools/quality_check/complexity.py's real run found sim/body/body.gd:242:_resolve_horizontal at cyclomatic complexity 24, the single highest in the 85-function GDScript corpus (IQR fence 6.0; the next-highest, sim/body/vertical_resolve.gd:23:move_and_resolve, is less than half that at 11). _resolve_horizontal directly contains ONE of the four controller defects docs/DECISIONS_LEDGER.md D0059 root-caused during the JUMP_CORNER investigation (the extends_forward step-up/mantle gating, sim/body/body.gd:267-274) -- verified against the current source, not assumed from the ledger's own function-name parenthetical, which names where the check lives but not how large a share of the function it is. The other three D0059 defects do NOT live in _resolve_horizontal: two (resolve_ceiling's failed-nudge-never-backs-out, and the corner-nudge's own missing world-bounds check) live in sim/body/vertical_resolve.gd::resolve_ceiling, called from move_and_resolve; the fourth was a test-harness blind spot (tests/test_reachability_sweep.gd), not production code. Of the three real-code sites, two (move_and_resolve at complexity 11, and grid_floor_backstop at complexity 10, both in vertical_resolve.gd) also appear in this run's own complexity outlier list -- but resolve_ceiling itself, the function containing two of the four defects, does NOT: its complexity sits at or below this run's 6.0 fence and is not printed. The correlation is real but partial: complexity flags 3 of 4 defect-adjacent functions across body.gd and vertical_resolve.gd (and names the single highest-complexity function in the whole corpus as one of them), but does not point to a single function containing all four defects, and misses the one site that hosted the most (resolve_ceiling, 2 of 4).
